requirements: The core contributions of QFlash — an end-to-end integer-only FlashAttention kernel — have been reproduced, including its integer softmax design, Triton kernel implementation, and evaluation on ViT/DeiT/Swin workloads.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware and software environment required to run QFlash has been correctly set up, including GPU, CUDA, PyTorch, Triton, TVM, and profiling tools.
GPU hardware requirements matching the paper's experimental setup have been established.

Code has been implemented to detect and require an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU (or compatible Blackwell architecture GPU supporting IMMA INT8 Tensor Cores) for reproducing the reported latency and energy results.

verification.spec: Inspect the repository for GPU capability detection logic (e.g., torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (12,0) or a device-name check for 'RTX 5090' / Blackwell) invoked at kernel-launch or benchmark-entry, and confirm that the code raises an error or logs a warning when run on non-Blackwell (SM<12.0) GPUs. Verify by importing the module on the target host and calling the detection function; also grep for capability checks in kernel/benchmark scripts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to verify the GPU supports both HMMA (FP16) and IMMA (INT8) Tensor Core instructions, since QFlash relies on IMMA and baselines rely on HMMA.

verification.spec: Load the environment verification module and call the Tensor Core capability check. It must confirm compute capability >= 7.5 for HMMA and >= 7.5 for IMMA (INT8). Verify by running a small torch.matmul with FP16 inputs and a small int8 GEMM (via torch._int_mm or triton kernel) and asserting both succeed without falling back to CUDA cores.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CUDA and PyTorch software stack has been installed at the versions specified in Section 5.
Code has been implemented to install/verify CUDA 12.8 as the CUDA toolkit version used with PyTorch.

verification.spec: Run `nvcc --version` (or read torch.version.cuda) and assert the CUDA toolkit version string starts with '12.8'. Also assert torch.version.cuda == '12.8'.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to install PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 12.8 support for running FlashAttention-2 (FP16) and Torch (FP32) baselines and hosting the Triton kernels.

verification.spec: Import torch and assert torch.__version__.startswith('2.7.1') and torch.version.cuda == '12.8' and torch.cuda.is_available() is True.

sub_tasks.requirements: Triton and TVM compiler frameworks have been installed at the versions used in the paper.
Code has been implemented to install Triton 3.3.1 for compiling and running the QFlash integer-only Triton kernel and FlashAttention-2 / INT-FlashAttention Triton implementations.

verification.spec: Import triton and assert triton.__version__ == '3.3.1'. Additionally, JIT-compile a minimal @triton.jit kernel and launch it on the GPU to confirm the toolchain works.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to install TVM 0.8 for compiling and running the I-ViT (TVM INT8) baseline kernel.

verification.spec: Import tvm and assert tvm.__version__.startswith('0.8'). Build a trivial tvm.tir schedule targeting CUDA to confirm the toolchain is functional.

sub_tasks.requirements: Profiling and measurement tooling for Tensor Core utilization and energy consumption has been installed and made available.
Code has been implemented to invoke NVIDIA Nsight Compute (ncu) to profile IMMA and HMMA Tensor Core utilization percentages for the attention kernels.

verification.spec: Locate the profiling script and confirm it invokes `ncu` (Nsight Compute) via subprocess with metrics such as `sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor_op_imma.sum` and `sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor_op_hmma.sum`. Run it on a tiny attention kernel and assert the produced report contains those metric names with numeric values.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to invoke nvidia-smi for sampling GPU power draw during kernel execution for the energy consumption experiment.

verification.spec: Locate the energy measurement script and confirm it launches `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw --format=csv --loop-ms=<N>` (or the pynvml equivalent) in a background thread/subprocess. Execute the sampler for 2 seconds during a dummy kernel and assert it produces a non-empty numeric time-series of power draw readings in watts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Runtime environment configuration for reproducible latency and accuracy measurement has been established.
Code has been implemented to configure CUDA event-based timing with warmup iterations and GPU synchronization for stable per-kernel latency measurement.

verification.spec: Implement a timing utility that uses `torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)` for start/end events, performs at least 10 warmup iterations (untimed), calls `torch.cuda.synchronize()` before start and after end, and averages at least 100 timed iterations. Verify by importing the utility, timing a trivial CUDA kernel, and confirming the reported latency is stable (coefficient of variation < 5% across 3 back-to-back runs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to set random seeds and deterministic flags for PyTorch/Triton so that SQNR, MSE, and Top-1 accuracy measurements are reproducible.

verification.spec: Implement a `set_seed(seed)` helper that sets `random.seed`, `numpy.random.seed`, `torch.manual_seed`, `torch.cuda.manual_seed_all`, `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True`, `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False`, and env var `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Verify by running the QFlash attention kernel twice with the same seed and identical INT8 Q/K/V inputs and asserting bit-exact output equality; then run with a different seed and assert reproducibility of the seed-specific output.

sub_tasks.requirements: The seven attention workloads (A1-A7) extracted from ViT, DeiT, and Swin models at 224x224 resolution have been correctly configured with the specified shapes, heads, context lengths, and head dimensions.
A workload configuration module exposing the seven attention shapes has been implemented with fields for #Win, H, N, D so downstream benchmark scripts can iterate over A1-A7.

Code has been implemented that defines a list/dict of seven workload entries labeled A1 through A7, each carrying the fields (#Win, H, N, D) and a resolved 4D shape tuple usable for allocating Q/K/V tensors.

verification.spec: Import the workloads module and access the workloads container (list/dict). Assert it contains exactly 7 entries keyed/named A1..A7. For each entry, assert the presence of fields ('num_windows' or '#Win', 'H', 'N', 'D') and a resolved 4D tuple 'shape' that can be passed to torch.randn to allocate Q/K/V tensors.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that flags whether each workload uses window partitioning (Swin-style) or not (ViT/DeiT-style), so batch-size handling can multiply the effective batch by #Win for A4-A7 and leave A1-A3 unchanged.

verification.spec: Implement a workload registry mapping A1..A7 to a dict containing keys `is_windowed: bool` and `num_windows: int` (with is_windowed=False for A1-A3, and is_windowed=True with num_windows in {64,16,4,1} for A4-A7). Verify by asserting the registry values match Table 1 and by calling an `effective_batch(workload, batch)` helper that returns `batch` for A1-A3 and `batch * num_windows` for A4-A7.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ViT/DeiT workloads A1-A3 have been configured with context length N=197 (196 patch tokens + 1 class token at 224x224 with 16x16 patches) and head dimension D=64.
Workload A1 (ViT/DeiT-Tiny source) is configured with #Win absent, H=3, N=197, D=64, giving a per-sample shape (3, 197, 64).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A1 entry. Assert H==3, N==197, D==64, and that #Win is None/absent (or 1). Assert the resolved per-sample shape equals (3, 197, 64).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload A2 (ViT/DeiT-Small source) is configured with #Win absent, H=6, N=197, D=64, giving a per-sample shape (6, 197, 64).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A2 entry. Assert H==6, N==197, D==64, #Win absent, and the resolved per-sample shape equals (6, 197, 64).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload A3 (ViT/DeiT-Base source) is configured with #Win absent, H=12, N=197, D=64, giving a per-sample shape (12, 197, 64).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A3 entry. Assert H==12, N==197, D==64, #Win absent, and the resolved per-sample shape equals (12, 197, 64).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Swin workloads A4-A7 have been configured with per-window context length N=49 (7x7 window at 224x224), head dimension D=32, and the correct #Win and H per stage.
Workload A4 (Swin-T/S Stage-1) is configured with #Win=64, H=3, N=49, D=32, giving a per-sample shape (64, 3, 49, 32).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A4 entry. Assert #Win==64, H==3, N==49, D==32, and resolved per-sample shape equals (64, 3, 49, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload A5 (Swin-T/S Stage-2) is configured with #Win=16, H=6, N=49, D=32, giving a per-sample shape (16, 6, 49, 32).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A5 entry. Assert #Win==16, H==6, N==49, D==32, and resolved per-sample shape equals (16, 6, 49, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload A6 (Swin-T/S Stage-3) is configured with #Win=4, H=12, N=49, D=32, giving a per-sample shape (4, 12, 49, 32).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A6 entry. Assert #Win==4, H==12, N==49, D==32, and resolved per-sample shape equals (4, 12, 49, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: Workload A7 (Swin-T/S Stage-4) is configured with #Win=1, H=24, N=49, D=32, giving a per-sample shape (1, 24, 49, 32).

verification.spec: From the workloads module, retrieve the A7 entry. Assert #Win==1, H==24, N==49, D==32, and resolved per-sample shape equals (1, 24, 49, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: The workload configuration supports both real-time (batch=1) and throughput (batch=8) evaluation modes as used in Section 5.

Code has been implemented that allows selecting batch size 1 or 8 (and optionally larger values such as 1024 used in Appendix A) for the A1-A7 workloads and correctly folds Swin's #Win into the effective batch dimension when allocating Q/K/V.

verification.spec: Implement a `make_qkv(workload, batch_size)` function that accepts batch_size in {1, 8, 1024} and workload id in {A1..A7}. It should allocate Q, K, V INT8 tensors on GPU with shape (batch_size * num_windows, H, N, D) taken from Table 1. Verify by calling it for (A2, batch=8) and asserting shape (8, 6, 197, 64), and for (A4, batch=8) and asserting shape (512, 3, 49, 32).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that materializes INT8 Q, K, V tensors of the correct dtype and shape for each (workload, batch_size) pair, matching the (batch * #Win, H, N, D) layout expected by the attention kernels under test.

verification.spec: For each (workload, batch_size) in the cross-product of {A1..A7} x {1, 8}, call the Q/K/V allocator and assert (a) dtype is torch.int8, (b) device is cuda, (c) shape equals (batch_size * num_windows, H, N, D) matching Table 1. Also assert values lie in [-128, 127].

sub_tasks.requirements: The workload definitions have been validated against the source models: A1-A3 shapes must match the actual attention layer shapes of ViT/DeiT-Tiny/Small/Base at 224x224, and A4-A7 must match the four Swin-T/S stages.

verification.spec: Load timm models `vit_tiny_patch16_224`, `vit_small_patch16_224`, `vit_base_patch16_224`, `deit_tiny_patch16_224`, `deit_small_patch16_224`, `deit_base_patch16_224`, `swin_tiny_patch4_window7_224`, `swin_small_patch4_window7_224`. For each ViT/DeiT model, run a dummy 224x224 image through the first attention block and assert the internal Q shape matches (H, N=197, D=64) from Table 1 with H in {3,6,12}. For each Swin model, iterate the four stages and assert the window-partitioned attention Q shape at stage k matches (num_windows_k, H_k, N=49, D=32) from A4-A7.

sub_tasks.requirements: The integer INT8xINT8->INT32 matrix multiplication used for Q-K score and P-V computation has been implemented following Equation (3).
The integer MatMul primitive supporting the QFlash pipeline has been implemented as a reusable component with correct shapes, dtypes, and scale bookkeeping.

Code has been implemented that defines an integer matrix multiplication routine (used for both step 1 Compute Query-Key MatMul and step 8 Compute Value MatMul) accepting two INT8 tensors and producing an INT32 output tensor.

verification.spec: Import the QFlash module and verify that a callable integer MatMul routine exists (e.g., `int_matmul` or equivalent function used within the Triton kernel). Use inspect/importlib to confirm the function exists, accepts two tensor arguments, and its signature/docstring or type annotations indicate INT8 inputs and INT32 output. Additionally invoke it with two small torch.int8 tensors and assert the output tensor has dtype torch.int32.

sub_tasks.requirements: The integer MatMul component accepts inputs shaped as A_hat in I_int8^{B_r x d} and B_hat in I_int8^{d x B_c} matching the tile shapes (B_r x d) and (d x B_c) defined in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Call the integer MatMul routine with A_hat of shape (B_r, d) and B_hat of shape (d, B_c) using representative tile sizes (e.g., B_r=64, d=64, B_c=64) with torch.int8 inputs. Assert the output tensor has shape (B_r, B_c). Additionally verify numerical correctness by comparing against a reference computation: output should equal A_hat.to(int32) @ B_hat.to(int32) exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The output accumulator dtype of the integer MatMul is INT32 (I_int32^{B_r x B_c}) so that the accumulation of INT8 products does not overflow within a single tile.

verification.spec: Invoke the integer MatMul with two INT8 tile-shaped tensors (e.g., B_r=64, d=64, B_c=64) filled with extreme values (e.g., all 127 or -128) that would overflow if accumulated in INT8 or INT16. Assert (a) the output dtype is torch.int32, and (b) the output values equal the reference torch.matmul(A.to(int32), B.to(int32)) exactly, confirming no overflow occurs within a tile.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Equation (3) scale semantics C_hat = A_hat . B_hat with s_C = s_A * s_B are correctly realized in code so that downstream steps consume a consistent scale.

Code has been implemented that computes or tracks the output scale s_C as the product of the two input scales s_A * s_B in accordance with Equation (3), either explicitly at the call site or symbolically as a precomputed constant fed to the kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash kernel launch code (host-side wrapper) and verify that for each integer MatMul (QK and PV) an output scale is computed or passed as s_C = s_A * s_B, either as an explicit Python multiplication before kernel launch or as a symbolic constant baked into the kernel constexpr. Grep the source for a line like `s_C = s_A * s_B` or equivalent scale-product computation feeding the requantization step.

sub_tasks.requirements: For step 1 (Q-K MatMul) the code uses s_A = s_Q and s_B = s_K so that the score tile S_hat carries the scale s_Q * s_K prior to any softmax scaling constant application.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash kernel wrapper and verify that the QK MatMul (step 1) is called with the Q tensor's scale as s_A and K tensor's scale as s_B, so the resulting INT32 score tile has effective scale s_Q * s_K prior to the softmax constant (log2(e)/sqrt(d)) being multiplied in. Confirm by locating the QK matmul call site and checking scale variable names/values.

sub_tasks.requirements: For step 8 (P-V MatMul) the code uses s_A = s_P (the requantized probability scale from step 6) and s_B = s_V so the numerator contribution tile carries the scale s_P * s_V.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash kernel and verify that the PV MatMul (step 8) uses the requantized probability tile P_hat (with scale s_P from step 6 Requantization) and the V tensor's scale s_V, producing a numerator contribution tile whose effective scale is s_P * s_V. Check the code path around Algorithm 1 line for step 8 and confirm the scale variables used.

sub_tasks.requirements: Deterministic numerical behavior of the integer MatMul has been verified against a reference implementation.

For random INT8 inputs A_hat and B_hat with tile shapes used in workloads A1-A7, the integer MatMul component produces INT32 outputs bit-exactly matching a reference torch.matmul on int32-casted operands (elementwise equality with zero tolerance).

verification.spec: For each workload A1..A7, allocate random INT8 tensors A_hat of shape (B_r, d) and B_hat of shape (d, B_c) using the tile sizes chosen by the QFlash kernel. Compute C_qflash = qflash_int_matmul(A_hat, B_hat) and C_ref = torch.matmul(A_hat.to(torch.int32), B_hat.to(torch.int32)). Assert torch.equal(C_qflash, C_ref) (bit-exact, zero tolerance) for all tested tile shapes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Dequantizing the INT32 output using s_C = s_A * s_B reconstructs the original floating-point matmul (A * s_A) @ (B * s_B) to within a small relative tolerance (e.g., < 1e-5) on random test tensors, confirming the scale relation from Equation (3).

verification.spec: Write a unit test that: (1) generates random FP matrices A_fp, B_fp; (2) quantizes them to INT8 with per-tensor scales s_A, s_B; (3) calls the QFlash INT8 matmul primitive to get C_int32; (4) computes C_reconstructed = C_int32 * s_A * s_B; (5) compares C_reconstructed to A_fp @ B_fp using relative error, asserting max relative error < 1e-2 (accounting for INT8 quantization noise) on tensors of size >=64x64.

sub_tasks.requirements: The integer MatMul is dispatched to Tensor Cores via IMMA instructions in the Triton implementation so that INT8 GEMM latency and utilization benefits are realized.

Code has been implemented such that the two MatMul calls in the QFlash Triton kernel invoke INT8 tensor-core paths (e.g., tl.dot with input_precision or dtype configuration producing IMMA), rather than falling back to CUDA-core integer or floating-point paths.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash Triton kernel source to confirm both tl.dot calls take int8 operands (tl.int8 inputs) and accumulate to int32. Then compile the kernel and dump the generated PTX/SASS (via triton's cache directory or TRITON_CACHE_DIR); grep for IMMA instructions (e.g., 'mma.sync.aligned.*.s8.s8.s32' in PTX or 'IMMA' in SASS) and verify at least one such instruction exists, and no HMMA (f16) mma instructions are present in the QK or PV matmul regions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The row-wise maximum computation and tile-wise running-max update mechanism has been implemented as specified in Section 4.2 and Equation (4).
The Compute Row-Max step (step 2 in Figure 2) has been implemented to extract per-row maxima from the INT32 QK score tile.
Code has been implemented that, given an INT32 score tile S_hat of shape (B_r x B_c), computes a row-wise maximum vector m_tilde of shape (B_r,) in INT32, as defined in Equation (4).

verification.spec: Locate the RowMax routine in the QFlash kernel module. Assert it is callable with signature accepting an INT32 tensor of shape (B_r, B_c) and returning an INT32 tensor of shape (B_r,). Inspect the Triton source and confirm use of tl.max(..., axis=1) or equivalent reduction with dtype=tl.int32.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the Row-Max operation is fused inside the Triton attention kernel and operates on on-chip tile data (SRAM/registers) without spilling the intermediate score tile to global memory.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel source and verify that Row-Max (step 2) is computed inline within the same kernel as the QK matmul (using tl.max over the tile), operating on the tile-local INT32 score buffer held in registers, with no intermediate tl.store of the full score tile to global memory between the matmul and the row-max reduction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Row-Max output values numerically match a reference torch.max(dim=-1) applied to the same INT32 tile (bit-exact equality) on representative random INT32 inputs.

verification.spec: Generate random INT32 tensors S of shape (B_r, B_c) for B_r in {16,32,64} and B_c in {16,32,64,128}. Call the QFlash row-max routine to get m_qflash and reference torch.max(S, dim=-1).values as m_ref. Assert torch.equal(m_qflash, m_ref) with zero tolerance across all tested shapes and random seeds (>=5 seeds each).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Update Max step (step 3 in Figure 2) has been implemented to maintain a running row-wise maximum across inner-loop tiles as described in Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1.

Code has been implemented that computes m_hat_i^(j) = max(m_hat_i^(j-1), m_tilde_i^(j)) elementwise per row, where m_hat_i^(j-1) is the running max from the previous inner-loop iteration and m_tilde_i^(j) is the current tile row-max.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel and verify presence of an elementwise `tl.maximum(m_prev, m_tile)` (or equivalent) call updating the running row-max, where m_prev is the running max carried across inner-loop iterations and m_tile is the current tile's row-max output. Confirm this occurs in step 3 (Update Max) of Algorithm 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The running max vector m_hat_i is initialized to the smallest representable INT32 value (or equivalent sentinel) at the start of each outer-loop iteration so that the first inner-tile max is correctly adopted.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel to confirm that at the start of each outer-loop iteration, the running max vector m_hat_i is initialized to INT32_MIN (or a comparable sentinel like -2**31 or a very negative constant such as float('-inf') cast to int). Locate the initialization line for m_i before the inner loop over Tc tiles.

sub_tasks.requirements: The running max m_hat_i is stored and updated in on-chip memory (kernel-local registers/shared memory) across the inner loop, without materializing it to HBM between inner-loop iterations.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel and verify that m_hat_i is declared as a kernel-local variable (via `tl.zeros` / `tl.full` / arithmetic assignment in register scope) and is NOT stored via `tl.store` to global memory (HBM) between inner-loop iterations. The running max should only be reused across iterations through register-level variable reassignment.

sub_tasks.requirements: The previous running max m_hat_i^(j-1) is preserved after the update so that it remains available for computing the Max-Offset Factor alpha (used in Score Intensity and numerator/denominator rescaling).

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel to verify that when updating the running max in step 3, the previous value m_hat_i^(j-1) is captured into a separate variable (e.g., `m_prev = m_i` before the update) so it can be used in step 5 (Max-Offset Factor computing alpha = exp(m_prev - m_new)) and in numerator rescaling. Confirm both m_prev and m_new are used in subsequent lines.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Row-Max / Update-Max implementation respects the per-tensor uniform scale requirement (Challenge C3) so that INT32 comparison across tiles is semantically valid.

Code has been implemented such that all QK score tiles compared in Update Max share the same scale factor s = s_Q * s_K * d^(-1/2) * log2(e) (a single per-tensor scalar), with no per-token or per-tile scale mismatch, and no dequantization is performed inside the Row-Max/Update-Max path.

verification.spec: Inspect the kernel and its wrapper: verify that s = s_Q * s_K * d^(-0.5) * log2(e) is computed once (as a Python-side scalar or kernel constexpr) and applied uniformly to all score tiles, with no per-token or per-row scale factor variation. Also verify no `dequantize`/cast-to-float operations occur inside the Row-Max or Update-Max code path.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that on a multi-tile QK score matrix, the QFlash tile-wise running max produced by Row-Max + Update-Max equals the full-matrix row-wise argmax value computed in one shot on the same INT32 data.

verification.spec: Write a unit test that: (1) constructs a random INT32 QK score matrix of size (Br*Tr) x (Bc*Tc), e.g., 128x256; (2) runs the QFlash kernel and extracts the final running max per row after all inner-loop iterations (e.g., via a debug hook or by isolating the Row-Max/Update-Max logic in a Python replica); (3) compares to `torch.max(score_matrix, dim=1).values` computed in one shot; (4) asserts elementwise equality.

sub_tasks.requirements: The GPU-friendly ShiftExp2 integer-only exponential approximation has been implemented using multiply-and-shift (avoiding integer division) as described in Section 4.3 and Algorithm 2.
The structural components of ShiftExp2 (function signature, constants, and control flow) exist in the codebase following Algorithm 2.

Code has been implemented providing a ShiftExp2 function (or Triton device function) that takes a quantized integer input x_hat and its scale s_x, and returns a quantized integer output y_hat with output scale s_y = s_x, matching the interface of Algorithm 2.

verification.spec: Locate the ShiftExp2 implementation (as a Triton `@triton.jit` device function, a Python helper, or an inline block within the main kernel). Verify its signature/interface accepts (x_hat, s_x) inputs and returns (y_hat, s_y) with s_y set equal to s_x, matching Algorithm 2 lines 3-11.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that guarantees ShiftExp2 is only applied to non-positive integer inputs (post row-max subtraction), consistent with the assumption in Section 4.3 that x_hat has negative values after Row-Max application.

verification.spec: Inspect the callers of ShiftExp2 in the QFlash kernel: verify that (1) in step 4 the input is (S_hat - m_hat_i) which is <= 0 by construction of row-max subtraction, and (2) in step 5 the input is (m_prev - m_new) which is <= 0 since m_new >= m_prev. Optionally add a `tl.static_assert` or runtime check that inputs are non-positive.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that constructs the effective scale s_tilde_X = s_X * log2(e) used to convert e^x into a base-2 power representation (Equation 5), and treats the integer/fractional decomposition consistently with x = q + r where q is a non-positive integer and r in (-1, 0].

verification.spec: Inspect the wrapper/host code and confirm that the score scale s = s_Q * s_K * d^(-0.5) * log2(e) is constructed (multiplication by log2(e) explicitly present) and used as the effective s_tilde_X input to ShiftExp2. Also verify the ShiftExp2 code decomposes x_hat into q (non-positive integer quotient) and r (remainder in (-1, 0]) via `q = (x_hat * M) >> N` and `r = x_hat + q * s_x_inv`, matching Equation (6).

sub_tasks.requirements: The multiply-and-shift replacement for integer division has been implemented as described in Equation (16) and Appendix B.2.

Code has been implemented that precomputes the fixed-point constant M = round((-s_x) * 2^N) outside the kernel (or as a compile-time constant), so that it depends only on the input scale and bit-width N and not on x_hat.

verification.spec: Inspect the host-side wrapper (Python code before kernel launch) and verify M is computed via `M = int(round((-s_x) * (2**N)))` (or equivalent) and passed as a scalar `constexpr` or kernel argument. Confirm M is NOT recomputed inside the kernel per element.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the quotient q = (x_hat * M) >> N using integer multiplication and an arithmetic right shift, avoiding any integer division inside the ShiftExp2 kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the source of the ShiftExp2 Triton kernel (via its .src attribute or by reading the file). Assert that: (1) the computation of q uses an integer multiplication by a precomputed constant M followed by tl.__rshift__ / '>>' operator; (2) neither '/' nor '//' nor tl.div / tl.floordiv appears in the q computation block. Confirm with a regex or AST scan.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ShiftExp2 implementation contains no integer division operator (e.g., `//`, `/` on integer types, or `tl.div_int`) anywhere in its hot path; only multiplication, addition, and shift operations are used.

verification.spec: Locate the ShiftExp2 implementation file(s) in the QFlash source (Triton kernel and any Python helpers). Parse the source and assert that within the ShiftExp2 function body there are no integer division tokens: no `//` operator, no `/` used on integer-typed variables, no `tl.div_int`, `tl.cdiv` on the hot path, no `divmod`, and no `%` (modulo) operator. Only `*`, `+`, `-`, `<<`, `>>`, `&`, `|` are permitted. Verified via AST inspection of the Python/Triton source of ShiftExp2.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that derives the remainder r = x_hat + q * s_x_inv (where s_x_inv = round(1/s_x)) so that the fractional part is recovered from the integer quotient rather than via a modulus operation.

verification.spec: Inspect the ShiftExp2 implementation and verify it computes `r = x_hat + q * s_x_inv` (using addition and multiplication) rather than using a modulo operator (`%`). sub_tasks.requirements: The linear approximation of the fractional exponential (Equation 7) and its combination with the integer part (Equation 8) have been implemented via shift operations.

verification.spec: Inspect the ShiftExp2 implementation and verify line 8 of Algorithm 2 is realized as `y_hat = ((r >> 1) + s_x_inv) >> (-q)` (with q non-positive so shift-right by |q| or equivalent, e.g., `>> q_abs` where q_abs = -q). Confirm the (r >> 1) + s_x_inv linear approximation of 2^r appears literally in the code, matching Equation (7).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces the final ShiftExp2 output y_hat = ((r >> 1) + s_x_inv) >> (-q), combining the linear fractional approximation with the integer exponent via a single right shift, consistent with Algorithm 2 line 8.

verification.spec: Inspect the ShiftExp2 source (Triton kernel and helpers). Assert that the final output expression matches the Algorithm 2 line 8 form: y_hat = ((r >> 1) + s_x_inv) >> (-q) (or equivalently `>> q` where q is negative/non-positive). Verify by AST/regex search that the last assignment to the output variable combines (r >> 1), an additive s_x_inv term, and a right-shift by a q-derived amount, in a single shift expression.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the output scale returned by ShiftExp2 satisfies s_y = s_x (as stated in Algorithm 2 line 9), so downstream ops (Score Intensity, Max-Offset Factor) can use the same scale without extra rescaling.

verification.spec: Inspect the ShiftExp2 return path (Algorithm 2 line 9-10) and verify that s_y is set equal to s_x (either returned as the same variable, or documented as such in comments/interface). Confirm downstream callers (Score Intensity step 4, Max-Offset Factor step 5) use this scale directly without additional rescaling before feeding into requantization or accumulation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Constants and reusable factors for ShiftExp2 are precomputed outside the kernel as prescribed in Section 4.3.

Code has been implemented that precomputes n, r (shift bits), and the fixed-point factor round(s_X/s_Y * 2^r) outside the Triton kernel, since these depend only on scale factors and bit-width and not on the runtime input tensor X_hat.

verification.spec: Inspect the host-side (Python) code that launches the Triton kernel and verify the following precomputations occur BEFORE the kernel call and are passed as kernel `constexpr` or scalar arguments: n (exponent for scale ratio), r (shift bits), and the fixed-point factor `round((s_X/s_Y) * 2**r)`. Grep for their computation lines outside `@triton.jit` scope.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that inside the kernel ShiftExp2 performs only element-wise integer arithmetic (multiplies, adds, shifts) on x_hat, with no per-element float computation or per-element scale-factor recomputation.

verification.spec: Inspect the ShiftExp2 body inside the Triton kernel and verify only integer ops appear: multiplication (`*`), addition (`+`), and bit-shifts (`>>`, `<<`). Confirm the absence of `tl.exp`, `tl.log`, float casts (`.to(tl.float32)`), or per-element division. Also confirm that scale factors (M, s_x_inv, log2(e), etc.) are passed as scalars, not recomputed per element.

sub_tasks.requirements: ShiftExp2 is used in the correct places within the QFlash pipeline (Score Intensity and Max-Offset Factor).
Code has been implemented that invokes ShiftExp2 in the Compute Score Intensity step (step 4) of Algorithm 1 to produce P_hat_i^(j) from S_hat_i^(j) - m_hat_i^(j) with the correct scale.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash kernel source and locate step 4 (Compute Score Intensity). Verify that after `S_hat_i^(j) - m_hat_i^(j)` is computed, ShiftExp2 (or the inline shift-exp block) is invoked on the result to produce P_hat_i^(j), with the effective scale s = s_Q * s_K * d^(-0.5) * log2(e).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that invokes ShiftExp2 in the Compute Max-Offset Factor step (step 5) of Algorithm 1 to produce alpha_hat_i^(j) = exp(m_hat_i^(j-1) - m_hat_i^(j)) using the same integer approximation path.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash kernel source and locate step 5 (Compute Max-Offset Factor). Verify that alpha_hat_i^(j) is computed by invoking ShiftExp2 (same integer path as step 4) on the input (m_hat_i^(j-1) - m_hat_i^(j)), producing an integer approximation of exp(m_prev - m_new).

sub_tasks.requirements: The ShiftExp2 implementation behaves correctly under unit-level tests against the reference exponential.
The ShiftExp2 function is monotonically non-decreasing over its supported non-positive integer input range for a fixed s_x, matching the monotonicity of the true exponential.

verification.spec: Write a unit test that: (1) fixes a scale s_x (e.g., 0.01); (2) iterates x_hat over all integer values in the supported non-positive range [x_min, 0] (or a dense sample if range is large); (3) calls ShiftExp2(x_hat, s_x) for each; (4) asserts the output sequence is monotonically non-decreasing as x_hat increases from x_min to 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: For inputs sampled from the range used in QFlash (post row-max negative integers), the ShiftExp2 approximation error relative to the true exp(x_hat * s_x) is small enough that the SQNR of ShiftExp2 alone on a random negative input tensor exceeds 30 dB, verifying the linear/shift approximation is implemented correctly.

verification.spec: Sample a random tensor of N=100000 negative integer inputs uniformly in the QFlash post-row-max range (e.g. int32 values corresponding to real values in [-20/s_x, 0] with s_x set by a typical QFlash softmax scale). Compute the ShiftExp2 approximation y_approx (dequantized to float) and the ground-truth y_true = exp(x_hat * s_x). Compute SQNR = 10*log10(sum(y_true^2) / sum((y_true - y_approx)^2)) and assert it exceeds 30 dB.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that the mul+shift computation q = (x_hat * M) >> N produces the same q (for all x_hat in the ShiftExp2 input range) as the reference integer-division definition q = floor(x_hat / s_x_inv), confirming that the division replacement is functionally equivalent.

verification.spec: Write a unit test that: (1) fixes s_x (e.g., 0.01), N (e.g., 15), computes s_x_inv = round(1/s_x) and M = round((-s_x) * 2**N); (2) iterates x_hat over the ShiftExp2 non-positive input range (e.g., [-1000, 0]); (3) computes q_mulshift = (x_hat * M) >> N and q_ref = -((-x_hat) // s_x_inv) (or equivalent floor-division reference); (4) asserts q_mulshift == q_ref for all tested x_hat. Note: exact equivalence may require sufficient N; if occasional off-by-one occurs the test should assert |q_mulshift - q_ref| <= 1 and document this.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fixed-point requantization from INT32 back to INT8 using multiplier M_r and shift bits r has been implemented as in Equations (9) and (10), enabling the pipeline to convert INT32 QK-score outputs into INT8 inputs for downstream ShiftExp2 and PV MatMul stages.
The requantization component exists as a well-defined operation in the QFlash Triton kernel with the correct interface.

Code has been implemented that provides a requantization operation taking an INT32 tile X_hat of shape [B_r, B_c] together with the fixed-point multiplier M_r and shift bits r, and returning an INT8 tile Y_hat of shape [B_r, B_c] as used in step 6 of Figure 2 and Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Import the requantization function from the QFlash implementation. Construct a random INT32 tile X_hat of shape [B_r=64, B_c=64] with values in a realistic post-GEMM range (e.g., int32 in [-2**20, 2**20]). Provide M_r and r consistent with Equation (9) for some s_in/s_out ratio. Call the function and assert: (1) output dtype is int8, (2) output shape is [64, 64], (3) values are within [-128, 127]. Compare against numpy reference (X_hat * M_r) >> r with clipping; max abs difference must be 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that precomputes the fixed-point multiplier M_r and shift bits r outside the Triton kernel from the input/output scale factors (using n = floor(log2(s_in / s_out)) and r chosen with respect to bit-width b) as described for Equation (9), so the kernel itself performs only integer multiply and shift.

verification.spec: Locate the QFlash host/setup code that prepares kernel arguments. Verify a Python helper function exists that, given (s_in, s_out, bit_width b), returns (M_r, r) with n = floor(log2(s_in/s_out)) and M_r = round((s_in/s_out) * 2**r). Call it with several (s_in, s_out) pairs and check (M_r/2**r) approximates (s_in/s_out) to within 2**-r relative error. Also verify by inspecting kernel launch that M_r and r are passed as scalar arguments (not recomputed inside the Triton kernel body).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the requantization step is invoked between the INT32 QK-score MatMul path and the ShiftExp2 / INT8 PV MatMul path inside the QFlash inner loop, matching step 6 in Figure 2 and Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Statically inspect the Triton QFlash kernel source. Verify the inner loop contains, in order: (a) an INT8xINT8->INT32 QK matmul (tl.dot with int8 inputs), (b) row-max update and score-intensity computation via ShiftExp2, (c) a requantization operation converting INT32 to INT8 using multiplier M_r and shift r, and (d) an INT8xINT8->INT32 PV matmul using the requantized P tile. Use regex/AST or textual scan to confirm ordering.

sub_tasks.requirements: The requantization component behaves deterministically according to Equations (9) and (10), using only integer multiplication and right-shift.
The multiplier is computed as M_r = round((s_in / s_out) * 2^r) for the chosen shift width r, following Equation (9), so that (s_in / s_out) is represented as a fixed-point value M_r / 2^r.

verification.spec: Unit-test the multiplier computation helper. For 20 random (s_in, s_out) pairs with s_in/s_out in [1e-4, 1e4] and r in {15, 16, 24, 31}, verify M_r == round((s_in/s_out) * 2**r) exactly (using Python's round()). Also verify M_r is a nonnegative integer representable in int32/int64 as appropriate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Requantization is performed as Y_hat = (X_hat * M_r) >> r using integer multiply-then-shift (no floating point and no integer division), matching Equation (10).

verification.spec: Locate the requantization step in the QFlash Triton kernel (Section 4.4, Eq. 10, step 6 in Figure 2). Assert via AST/regex that the requantization is implemented as `(X_hat * M_r) >> r` on integer tensors: (a) M_r and r are integer constants precomputed outside the kernel, (b) no floating-point cast to float16/float32 is present in the requantization block, (c) no integer division (`//`, `/`, `tl.cdiv`, `%`) is used.

sub_tasks.requirements: The requantized output is clipped/saturated into the signed INT8 range Iint(8) = [-2^7, 2^7 - 1] before being returned, ensuring the result is a valid INT8 tensor for the subsequent ShiftExp2 and PV MatMul stages.

verification.spec: Call the requantization function with INT32 inputs deliberately chosen so that the raw (X_hat*M_r)>>r result exceeds [-128, 127] (e.g., large positive and negative values). Assert every returned element is in [-128, 127] and dtype is int8. Also verify that inputs that would map exactly to values in-range are not modified (no spurious saturation on safe inputs).

sub_tasks.requirements: After requantization, the tracked output scale s_out is used consistently by downstream stages (ShiftExp2, row-sum, PV MatMul), so that s_in / s_out ~ M_r / 2^r holds and the represented real-valued tensor is preserved up to fixed-point rounding.

verification.spec: Run the full QFlash kernel end-to-end on a small workload (e.g., N=128, d=64, single head). Instrument or inspect the code to extract the scale tracked before requantization (s_in) and after (s_out). Compute the represented real-valued tensor P_real = P_int8 * s_out and compare to the pre-requant real-valued tensor S_real = S_int32 * s_in. Assert max relative error <= 1/(2**(r-1)) plus quantization noise, confirming s_in/s_out ~ M_r/2**r is preserved.

sub_tasks.requirements: Numerical validation confirms that the mul+shift requantization matches the reference floating-point rescaling to within quantization error on realistic QFlash tiles.

Report max absolute difference per tile; median across tiles should be <= 1 (quantization LSB) and worst-case <= 2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel partitions Q into T_r = ceil(N/B_r) blocks of size B_r x d and K, V into T_c = ceil(N/B_c) blocks of size B_c x d, using program_id to index the outer Q-tile loop as described in Algorithm 1 line 2.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel source: verify that grid launch computes T_r = ceil(N/B_r) programs along the Q-tile axis, that program_id(0) indexes the outer Q-tile, and that Q is loaded in [B_r, d] tiles while K, V are loaded in [B_c, d] tiles. Run with N not divisible by B_r/B_c to ensure ceil rounding is used (mask handling present).

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel implements an outer loop over Q-tiles i in [1, T_r] (parallelized across programs) and an inner loop over K/V-tiles j in [1, T_c] that sequentially performs the eleven steps of Figure 2 for each (i, j) pair.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel: confirm there is an outer parallel dimension over i in [0, T_r) via program_id, and a sequential for-loop over j in range(T_c) inside the kernel body. Within the j-loop, verify the eleven Figure-2 steps appear in code (matmul QK, rowmax, update max, shift-exp, alpha, requant, rowsum, matmul PV, l accumulate, O accumulate) before the loop exits.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel uses per-tensor quantization scales (single scalar s_Q, s_K, s_V per tensor) rather than per-token or per-head scales, so tile-wise integer comparison in the Update Max step is done directly on INT32 values without dequantization.

verification.spec: Check the kernel signature and wrapper: s_Q, s_K, s_V must be passed as Python scalars (float) rather than tensors of length N or H. Verify no per-token/per-head scale tensor is loaded inside the kernel and that the UpdateMax step compares INT32 partial-max values directly without any dequant to float.

sub_tasks.requirements: The eleven steps of Figure 2 are all present in the kernel body in the correct order and correctly wired via on-chip SRAM buffers.

Within each inner iteration, the code executes steps in the order (1) Q-K MatMul -> (2) RowMax -> (3) UpdateMax -> (4) Score Intensity ShiftExp2 -> (5) Max-Offset Factor alpha_i -> (6) Requantization to INT8 P -> (7) RowSum -> (8) P-V MatMul -> (9) Accumulate Denominator l -> (10) Accumulate Numerator O -> and after the inner loop closes, (11) Normalize.

verification.spec: Static analysis of the kernel body: identify the 11 steps by inspecting the source and confirm they appear in the exact order QK-matmul, rowmax, update-max, shift-exp2 on S, compute alpha via shift-exp2 on (m_prev - m_new), requant S to INT8 P, rowsum on P, PV-matmul, l = alpha*l_prev + rowsum, O = alpha*O_prev + P@V, followed by normalize after loop.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel maintains on-chip per-row accumulator state m_i (running max, INT32), l_i (denominator, INT32), and O_i (numerator, INT32) across inner-loop iterations without writing intermediate S or P tiles to off-chip memory.

verification.spec: Inspect Triton kernel: verify m_i, l_i, and O_i are declared as tl.zeros/tl.full accumulators inside the kernel (register/SRAM resident) and only tl.store is called after the inner loop finishes. Confirm no tl.store of S or P tiles occurs inside the j-loop.

sub_tasks.requirements: Before the inner loop, m_i is initialized to the minimum representable INT32 (or a suitably small sentinel), and l_i and O_i are initialized to zero as INT32 accumulators.

verification.spec: Inspect the kernel: locate initialization of m_i (should be tl.full with INT32 min or a very negative sentinel like -2**31 or -1e9 cast to int32), and l_i, O_i initialized via tl.zeros with dtype tl.int32.

sub_tasks.requirements: After the outer loop over inner tiles completes, the kernel writes the final INT8 output tile O_i for the assigned Q-block to global memory exactly once, and does not write intermediate S, P, l, or m tensors to global memory.

verification.spec: Inspect the kernel: confirm exactly one tl.store call targeting the O output pointer occurs after the inner j-loop, writing a [B_r, d] INT8 tile. Verify no tl.store for S, P, l, or m tensors is present anywhere in the kernel.

sub_tasks.requirements: The full kernel executes entirely in the integer domain, with no floating-point exp, division, or softmax normalization inside the fused kernel.

Inspection of the compiled Triton kernel (or its source) shows no FP16/FP32 arithmetic on the S, P, l, O accumulators or in the softmax path; only INT8/INT32 tl.dot, integer add/sub, integer multiply, and bit-shift operations are used inside the inner loop.

verification.spec: Parse the Triton kernel source and assert that (a) all tl.dot calls use INT8 inputs with INT32 accumulator (out_dtype=tl.int32); (b) no tl.float16/tl.float32 dtypes appear on S, P, l, m, O accumulators inside the inner loop; (c) softmax path uses only integer add/sub/mul and bit-shifts (<<, >>). Fail if any float cast is found on these tensors.

sub_tasks.requirements: The final normalization step 11 (O_i / l_i) is implemented using integer arithmetic (e.g., integer multiply by reciprocal approximation plus shift) and produces INT8 outputs directly, without invoking floating-point division.

verification.spec: Inspect the normalization step 11: verify O_i / l_i is implemented with an integer reciprocal approximation (multiply by fixed-point inverse of l_i then right-shift), and that the final store dtype is tl.int8. No tl.float32 division should be present.

sub_tasks.requirements: Constants that depend only on scales and bit widths (n, r, M_r, floor(s_tilde_X), floor(s_X_inv), and floor(s_Y / (s_X * 2^r) )) are precomputed outside the kernel and passed in as scalar arguments, so the kernel body performs only element-wise integer ops as described in Section 4.3 and Section 4.4.

verification.spec: Inspect the Python wrapper: verify constants n, r, M_r, floor(s_tilde_X), floor(s_X_inv), and floor(s_Y/(s_X*2^r)) are computed on the host from scalar scales and passed as constexpr/scalar kernel arguments. Confirm none of these are computed inside the kernel body per iteration.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the INT8 output tensor produced by the QFlash attention kernel is dequantized back to FP32 (using the appropriate output scale factor) so that it can be consumed by downstream FP32 layers in the ViT/DeiT/Swin inference pipeline (attention-only quantization setup)

verification.spec: Construct small random FP32 Q, K, V tensors (e.g., shape (1, 3, 32, 64)). Run the reference FP32 attention: O_ref = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(D)) @ V. Then run the end-to-end QFlash path: dynamically quantize Q, K, V to INT8, run the QFlash kernel to get INT8 output plus an output scale, and dequantize to FP32 via O_qflash = int8_out.float() * s_out. Assert (1) O_qflash has dtype float32, (2) O_qflash.shape == O_ref.shape, (3) cosine similarity between O_qflash.flatten() and O_ref.flatten() > 0.98, and (4) SQNR = 10*log10(||O_ref||^2 / ||O_ref - O_qflash||^2) > 25 dB (consistent with paper's reported >30 dB on realistic workloads, with margin for tiny test size).
verification.paper_cite: Section 5.3: 'we quantize only the attention modules while keeping the remaining layers in floating point'; Section 4.7: 'we implement this division entirely in integer arithmetic ... producing int8 outputs directly usable for downstream computation.'

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)

Code has been implemented such that Step 4 (Compute Score Intensity) applies ShiftExp2 to the tile (S_hat - m_hat) using the composite softmax scale s = s_Q * s_K * d^{-1/2} * log2(e), yielding an INT32 attention-strength tile.

verification.spec: Construct a small tile S_hat (INT32, shape [Br,Bc]) with known q,k scales and d; compute m_hat = rowmax(S_hat); call the implementation's score-intensity routine; compare its output to reference float exp((S_hat - m_hat) * s_Q*s_K/sqrt(d)) requantized; assert element-wise relative error < 0.05 and SQNR > 25 dB.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 5 (Compute Max-Offset Factor) computes alpha_hat = ShiftExp2(m_prev - m_new) using integer arithmetic to rescale prior tile results.

verification.spec: Feed pairs (m_prev, m_new) with m_prev <= m_new; call the Max-Offset Factor routine; compare integer alpha_hat/scale to float exp(m_prev - m_new); assert max relative error < 0.05 over 100 random pairs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 6 (Requantization) converts an INT32 tile to INT8 via a fixed-point multiplier M_r and shift r, as specified in Eqs. (9)-(10).

verification.spec: Given input INT32 tensor X with source scale s_X and target scale s_Y, compute M_r = round((s_X/s_Y)*2^r) and expected Y = clip((X*M_r) >> r, -128, 127); call implementation's requantize function; assert output equals expected exactly for at least 1000 random elements and dtype is int8.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 7 computes the row-sum of the INT8 probability tile P into an INT32 accumulator per row.

verification.spec: Create a random INT8 tile P of shape [Br,Bc]; call implementation's row-sum kernel; assert output dtype is int32, shape [Br], and values equal P.sum(dim=1) computed in int64 reference.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 9 accumulates the denominator as l_hat := alpha_hat * l_prev + rowsum(P) using integer-only arithmetic without floating-point conversion.

verification.spec: Simulate a sequence of tile updates with known alpha_hat and rowsum(P) values; call the denominator accumulator; assert final integer l_hat matches a reference computation performed in int64, and inspect the kernel/function source to confirm no float dtype is used.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 10 accumulates the numerator as O_hat := alpha_hat * O_prev + P_hat @ V_hat using the ScaleRelease strategy that keeps O_hat's scale constant across tiles.

verification.spec: Run the numerator accumulator over 8 successive tiles with random INT8 P,V; verify that the associated scale for O_hat remains constant (Scale Release) across iterations, and that the accumulated integer O_hat, when divided by the constant scale, matches a float reference within relative error 0.1 and SQNR > 20 dB.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that Step 11 performs the final softmax normalization O_final = numerator / denominator entirely in integer arithmetic and returns INT8 outputs.

verification.spec: Given final accumulated numerator O_hat (INT32) and denominator l_hat (INT32) plus scale metadata, call the normalize routine; assert output dtype is int8, output range within [-128,127], and dequantized result matches reference softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V with SQNR > 25 dB on a small random Q,K,V; also inspect implementation to confirm no float division is used.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that s_tilde_X = s_X * log2(e) is precomputed outside the Triton kernel and passed in as an integer/fixed-point constant.

verification.spec: Inspect the QFlash launch/wrapper code and confirm that a constant equal to round(s_X * log2(e)) (or an equivalent precomputed fixed-point tilde-scale) is computed on the host side and forwarded as a kernel argument; assert the Triton kernel body does not call log2 or math.log.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the quotient q in ShiftExp2 is computed as q = (x_hat * M) >> N with a fixed-point multiplier M, avoiding integer division on GPU.

verification.spec: Instantiate the ShiftExp2 helper for a range of negative x_hat inputs; extract the quotient q it computes; assert q equals floor((x_hat * M) >> N) where M = round((-s_x) * 2^N); also inspect kernel source to confirm no integer division operator (//, tl.floor_divide) appears in the quotient computation path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that ShiftExp2 computes remainder r = x_hat + q * s_inv_x and approximates the fractional exponential as 2^r ≈ (r>>1) + s_inv_x (Eq. 7).

verification.spec: For 100 random negative x_hat inputs with given s_x, compute the implementation's intermediate r and fractional approximation; assert r lies in (-s_inv_x, 0]; assert the fractional approximation equals (r>>1) + s_inv_x; and confirm the approximation error vs. true 2^(r/s_inv_x) is bounded (max abs error < 0.06).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the final ShiftExp2 output y_hat = ((r>>1)+s_inv_x) >> q matches a reference exponential within tolerance across the used input range.

verification.spec: Run ShiftExp2 on 10000 uniformly sampled x_hat in [-128*s_inv_x, 0]; dequantize the integer output y_hat by scale s_y; compute SQNR against reference exp(x_hat/s_x); assert SQNR is close to the paper's reported ShiftExp2 fidelity (target 30 dB, tolerance 0.20 relative).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the fixed-point multiplier M_r = round((s_X / s_Y) * 2^r) is precomputed outside the Triton kernel and passed in as a constant, rather than being computed per-tile inside the kernel.

verification.spec: Import the QFlash implementation; locate the host-side setup routine that prepares kernel arguments (e.g., a `prepare_qflash_args` or the wrapper calling the Triton kernel). Call it with representative s_Q, s_K, s_V, and shift bit-width r. Assert that the returned/passed multiplier equals round((s_X / s_Y) * 2**r) for the requantization step (Eq. 9). Also assert that the Triton kernel signature accepts M_r (and n, r) as scalar arguments and does not recompute them from float scales inside the kernel body (inspect kernel source text for absence of float division on s_X/s_Y).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that requantization from INT32 to INT8 is performed as Y_hat = (X_hat * M_r) >> r, using only integer multiplication and arithmetic right shift (Equation 10).

verification.spec: Import the requantization helper (or invoke the QFlash kernel on a synthetic INT32 tile of shape (Br, Bc)=(64,64) with known M_r and r). Compare the output against a reference numpy implementation ref = (X_hat.astype(int64) * M_r) >> r cast to int8. Assert element-wise equality for at least 1000 random inputs sampled uniformly from int32 range scaled to avoid overflow. Also grep the Triton kernel source for a right-shift operator (>>) applied after an int multiplication with M_r.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the INT8 requantization output is saturated/clipped into the signed 8-bit range [-128, 127] before being used in downstream INT8 GEMMs.

verification.spec: Feed the requantization routine (or full QFlash kernel with a controlled tile) an INT32 input tile designed so that (X_hat * M_r) >> r would exceed 127 and go below -128 (e.g., set X_hat entries to +2^28 and -2^28 with M_r/r that map them outside int8). Verify that the output tensor's dtype is int8 and that no element exceeds 127 or falls below -128. Additionally assert that values that would overflow are clamped exactly to 127 or -128 (not wrapped around modulo 256).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that ScaleRelease approximates the inverse of the exponential scale as an integer (fixed-point) so that the P_hat @ V_hat contribution can be divided/rescaled without floating-point operations before accumulation into the numerator.

verification.spec: Locate the ScaleRelease routine referenced in Section 4.6 / Appendix B.1. Confirm via source inspection that the inverse-scale term is materialized as an integer multiplier + shift (no float32/float16 dtype appears in this code path inside the Triton kernel). Then run it on a small synthetic tile and compare against a floating-point reference: for random INT32 P_hat @ V_hat outputs and known scales, the integer ScaleRelease result must agree with the float reference within relative error <= 1e-2. Also verify that the accumulator dtype used after ScaleRelease is int32, not float.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the numerator update O_hat := alpha_hat * O_prev + P_hat @ V_hat is performed entirely with integer arithmetic (no float32/float16 intermediate tensors) in the QFlash Triton kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel source for the 'Accumulate Numerator' block (step 10 in Algorithm 1). Assert that: (1) the O accumulator tl.zeros(...) is declared with dtype tl.int32 (not float); (2) alpha_hat is applied via integer multiply-and-shift (search for '>>' following a multiplication with an alpha-related variable); (3) P_hat @ V_hat is computed with tl.dot(..., out_dtype=tl.int32) using int8 inputs. Then run the kernel end-to-end on workload A1 (batch=1, 3 heads, N=197, D=64) with random int8 Q/K/V and verify the resulting O is int8 or int32 (not float), and that outputs are bit-exact reproducible across two runs with the same seed (deterministic integer path).
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.6, Algorithm 1 line for Accumulate Numerator

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the denominator update l_hat := alpha_hat * l_prev + rowsum(P_hat) is performed entirely with integer arithmetic (no float32/float16 intermediate scalars) in the QFlash Triton kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the Triton kernel source for the 'Accumulate Denominator' block (step 9 in Algorithm 1). Assert that: (1) the l accumulator is declared with tl.int32 dtype; (2) rowsum over P_hat is computed with tl.sum on an int8/int32 tensor; (3) alpha_hat is applied to l_prev via integer multiply-and-shift (no float cast). sub_tasks.requirements: Ablation studies from the paper

Code has been implemented and run such that the step-wise integer optimization V4 (QK+PV INT8 GEMMs + integer exp + tile-wise integer accumulation) achieves 62.4% speedup over FlashAttention-2 baseline (V0) on workload A2 batch 1024.

verification.spec: Run V0 (FP FlashAttention-2 baseline) and V4 (fully integer QFlash) on workload A2 with batch size 1024; compute speedup fraction = (V0_latency - V4_latency)/V0_latency; assert |measured - 0.624| / 0.624 <= tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that step-wise application of integer operations to the FlashAttention-2 kernel (V0 baseline, V1 QK INT8 GEMM, V2 + PV INT8 GEMM, V3 + integer-approximated exp, V4 + integer tile accumulation) is measured on workload A2 with batch size 1024, and each successive version yields the reported cumulative speedup (V1: ~41.4%, V2: ~46.0%, V3: ~61.0%, V4: ~62.4%).

verification.spec: Implement/obtain the five kernel variants V0-V4; run on workload A2 batch=1024; compute speedup = (lat_V0 - lat_Vk)/lat_V0; assert V4 speedup within tolerance of 0.624.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the Scale Accumulation vs Scale Release ablation demonstrates monotonically decreasing SQNR across inner-loop iterations, with Scale Release remaining substantially higher (more stable) than Scale Accumulation as iteration count grows to 16.

verification.spec: Implement both scale-management schemes for integer tile accumulation; run inner loop for iterations {1..16}; compute SQNR vs FP32 reference at each step; assert SQNR(ScaleRelease@16) - SQNR(ScaleAccumulation@16) >= 10 dB (Scale Release clearly more stable).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that integer division throughput vs (int*int)>>int (mul+shift) throughput is benchmarked on GPU, and mul+shift shows substantially higher elements/second than integer division.

verification.spec: Write a Triton or CUDA microbenchmark computing int//int vs (int*int)>>N over ~4e6 elements; measure elements/s; assert mul+shift throughput > int_div throughput by at least 1.5x (paper shows roughly 3e11 vs 2e11).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that per-tensor, per-head, and per-token quantization granularities are compared for attention, demonstrating that per-token granularity produces mismatched tile-wise scales that break integer-only accumulation while per-tensor/per-head maintain uniform scales.

verification.spec: Instantiate Q,K tiles with random values, compute per-tensor / per-head / per-token quantization scales; verify per-tensor yields a single scalar scale, per-head yields H scales, per-token yields N scales; check that concatenating per-token QK^T tile outputs requires per-tile rescale, whereas per-tensor path does not.

verification.spec: Instantiate INT-FlashAttention (Half-precision variant) as described in Chen et al. 2024; run it on random INT8 Q,K,V tensors of shape (batch=8, heads=6, N=197, D=64) with a fixed seed; compute the reference FP32 attention output; measure SQNR = 10*log10(sum(ref^2)/sum((ref-out)^2)); assert |measured_sqnr - 38.19| / 38.19 <= 0.20
